title: Pitch & Protecting Our Ears
source: Science G3 B2 Study sheet pp.17-22; Worksheet Q13

scenes.t: Pitch is how high or low a sound is. It depends on how fast something vibrates.
Fast vibrations make a high-pitched sound, like a bird chirping, a violin, a whistle or a woman's voice.
Slow vibrations make a low-pitched sound, like a lion roaring, a drum, heart beats or a man's voice.
Tightness changes pitch. Tighten a drum skin for a higher pitch. Loosen it for a lower pitch.
Length changes pitch. Short guitar strings make a high pitch. Long strings make a low pitch.
Air changes pitch too. Blow across a bottle with little air space and you get a high pitch. More air space gives a lower pitch.
Sound travels easily through hard materials like wood and metal. Soft materials like foam, rubber and cotton wool muffle, or reduce, sound.
Loud sounds for a long time can damage our ears. Turn the volume down, wear ear defenders or ear plugs, and spend less time near loud noise.

activities.prompt: Is it a HIGH or LOW pitched sound?

why.h: Fast vibrations, short, tight or little air.
why.w: Slow vibrations, long, loose or more air.

activities.title: Sound Through or Muffled?
activities.prompt: Does sound travel easily through it, or is it muffled?

why.t: Hard materials like wood and metal carry sound.
why.m: Soft materials absorb and reduce sound.

activities.title: Water Bottle Music
activities.goal: Make high and low notes with bottles.
need: 3 glass bottles or glasses the same size

predict.q: Which bottle will make the HIGHEST sound when you blow across it?
o: The one with the most water
The one with the least water

steps.t: Fill one bottle a little, one half full, and one almost full.
Blow gently across the top of each bottle. Listen to the pitch.
Which one is highest? Which one is lowest? Put them in order.
Bonus: tap each bottle gently with a spoon and listen again!

activities.result: When you blow, the bottle with the most water (little air) makes the highest note, and the one with the least water makes the lowest.
activities.why: Less air space vibrates quickly for a high pitch. More air space vibrates slowly for a low pitch.
